subject: physics
question_text: Distinguish between fundamental units and derived units.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Fundamental units
lines: The units of the fundamental quantities are
steps.why: Independent means no fundamental unit can be built from the others. That independence is why exactly seven of them are enough to define every other unit.
common_mistakes: Giving newton or joule as a fundamental unit. Both are built from metre, kilogram and second.

recall.must_convey: That fundamental units are the units of the fundamental quantities and are independent, such as metre, kilogram and second.

steps.memory_tip: Fundamental units stand alone. Metre, kilogram, second — nothing builds them.
steps.margin_note: Write the examples. They carry the mark as much as the definition.

steps.label: Derived units

lines.text: Derived units are built from fundamental units

lines: They are the units of derived quantities.
steps.why: Writing newton as kg m s⁻² shows the derivation in one line, which is exactly what "derived" means.
common_mistakes: Naming a derived unit without showing what it is built from.

Calling kilometre, centimetre or gram a derived unit. A prefix makes a multiple or sub-multiple of one fundamental unit, not a derived unit. A derived unit combines fundamental units, like kg m s⁻². Kilogram itself is the base unit.

recall.must_convey: That derived units are the units of derived quantities, built from fundamental units, such as newton and joule.

steps.memory_tip: Write newton = kg m s⁻². One line proves the word "derived".
steps.margin_note: The kg m s⁻² line is worth writing — it is the proof.

insider_note: Both books ask this. Give one example with each definition — the example is what shows you understood it.
